runtime: Python 3.13/3.14 on supported Windows 10/11 Beta targets

xlsx_stack.preflight: Python stdlib os/pathlib/stat + zipfile performs path/reparse/stability/container/resource/part-name/content-type/relationship preflight before workbook library opens the file
xlsx_stack.semantic_reader: openpyxl in read-only streaming mode with formulas not evaluated and external links disabled; exact compatible package version is pinned by LLD-12/release lock after Python 3.13/3.14 compatibility matrix passes
rules: openpyxl is never exposed to a file that failed ZIP/resource/XML-active-content preflight
semantic formula cells are rejected; no cached formula result becomes accepted source value
no macro-enabled workbook or embedded executable content is accepted
adapter code wraps library objects immediately into bounded primitive parser values and never persists workbook/cell objects

why_not_custom_ooxml: Beta does not implement a bespoke general XLSX engine. Security-critical package preflight is small and explicit, while worksheet/date/style decoding uses a mature reader behind strict resource/profile tests. This reduces custom parsing surface without granting the library authority to execute formulas or fetch resources.
concurrency: Discovery/parsing/fingerprinting/proposal computation runs outside authoritative writer transactions; database staging batches are bounded. Domain acceptance remains short serialized LLD-01 UnitOfWork mutations.
dependency_gate: Before implementation acceptance, the pinned workbook-library version must pass the full LLD-04 malicious/large/golden fixture suite on both supported Python versions. A dependency upgrade is not semantic authority and requires replaying those fixtures.
